checks_performed: Read only the authorized source JSON and draft JSON; no web or other research files were consulted.
Compared the exact unconditional all-c target against the draft's stated scope and final writeup.
Reconstructed proofs for exact-size domination, greedy coverage and repair, sparse deletion certificates, edge-edit Lipschitz transfer, additive approximation, and the Vertex Cover gadget.
Audited boundary cases q=0, q=1, q=n, and n=0. The displayed greedy bound in claim 2 is necessarily used on its q≥1 domain; q=0 is separately trivial.

Ran the persisted integer-only checker. It exhaustively checked 1,100 graphs through five vertices, 6,505 graph-threshold pairs, 32,767 sparse witness subsets, 4,166 ordered graph pairs, 34,570 constructive transfers, 41,502 gap cases, 558 isolate-free degree-three gadget inputs, and 362,528 gadget dominating-set conversions.
Audited the PTAS and P-versus-NP implications deductively. The cited cubic-Vertex-Cover APX-hardness result was treated only as the explicit hypothesis of claim 12, not independently sourced.

claims.claim: For 0≤q≤n, a graph has a dominating set of exactly q vertices if and only if its domination number γ is at most q.
claims.evidence: An exact-q dominating set immediately gives γ≤q. Conversely, a minimum dominating set of size γ≤q can be enlarged by q−γ unused vertices because q≤n, and domination is preserved by supersets. This also covers n=q=0.
claims.search_method: Direct proof from monotonicity of domination, corroborated by exhaustive labeled-graph enumeration through n=5.

claims.claim: Greedy closed-neighborhood coverage has residual r≤n(1-1/q)^q whenever γ(G)≤q, for q≥1.
claims.evidence: Extend a minimum dominating set to a q-set D. For each current uncovered set U, the q sets N[d]∩U cover U, so one has size at least |U|/q. If U is nonempty that vertex is unselected, since a selected vertex's closed neighborhood is already covered. Greedy therefore leaves at most (1−1/q)|U| per round, yielding the claimed bound after q rounds.
claims.search_method: Averaging proof with integer cross-multiplication r q^q≤n(q−1)^q; exhaustively checked through n=5.

claims.claim: For arbitrary fixed c, greedy gives an exact polynomial-time triage: it solves the instance whenever r≤n/c or r>n(1-1/q)^q.
claims.evidence: On the displayed formula's q≥1 domain, if r≤n/c, every residual vertex u is outside the selected q-set S and has no edge to any s∈S. Adding su for one fixed s∈S therefore uses exactly r edits and makes S dominating. If r exceeds the bound, claim 1's contrapositive gives γ(G)>q, so (G,nil) is correct. Integer powers give an exact polynomial-size comparison; comparison with n/c is governed by the source's stated computability requirement for the radius. The q=0 input is separately solved without invoking this formula.
claims.search_method: Constructive branch proof and exact exhaustive checks for several rational constants on all graphs through n=5.

claims.claim: Sidestep(Dominating Set,dist_e,n/c) is in FP for every fixed c≤e.
claims.evidence: For q≥1, (1−1/q)^q≤e^−1. Thus either the residual violates claim 1's bound, giving a correct nil output on G, or r≤n/e≤n/c and claim 2 repairs it within radius. For q=0, the empty set is valid exactly when n=0; otherwise nil on G is correct. All constructions preserve the vertex set and q.
claims.search_method: Analytic inequality plus the exact constructive checks of the greedy and repair branches.

claims.claim: For every c, all instances with q≥1 and n-q≤n/c have a direct polynomial-time YES output.
claims.evidence: Choose any q-set S and s∈S. Only vertices outside S can be undominated. For each such vertex u, add su if needed; that edge was absent because u was undominated. At most n−q edges are added, and S then dominates the resulting graph.
claims.search_method: Direct construction, exhaustively checked for every threshold on all graphs through n=5.

claims.claim: For every c, a computable sparse NO certificate is available when q+1 vertices have at most n/c incident edges in total.
claims.evidence: Given such a set X of q+1 vertices, delete the union of edges incident with X. This uses at most n/c edits and makes every vertex of X isolated, forcing every dominating set to contain all q+1 vertices. Thus no exact q-set exists. The sum of degrees upper-bounds the incident-edge union, so selecting the q+1 lowest-degree vertices gives the stated efficiently computable sufficient certificate.
claims.search_method: Constructive proof; all 32,767 nonempty witness subsets arising in exhaustive graphs through n=5 were checked exactly.

claims.claim: Domination number is one-Lipschitz per edge edit, with a constructive transfer.
claims.evidence: If S dominates H, let U be the vertices it fails to dominate in G. Each u∈U is dominated in H through a distinct edge from S belonging to E(H)\E(G), hence |U|≤|E(H)\E(G)|. The set S∪U dominates G. Applying this in both directions to minimum dominating sets yields |γ(G)−γ(H)|≤|E(G)△E(H)|.
claims.search_method: Bidirectional constructive proof, corroborated on every ordered pair of labeled graphs through n=4 and 34,570 dominating-set transfers.

claims.claim: A radius-R sidestep solver decides every additive-gap instance whose YES case has γ(G)≤q-R and whose NO case has γ(G)>q+R.
claims.evidence: For every returned H with distance d≤R, the Lipschitz bound gives γ(H)≤γ(G)+d≤q in the YES case and γ(H)≥γ(G)−d>q in the NO case. Therefore every graph in the permitted ball has the same output type, so inspecting set versus nil decides the promise instance.
claims.search_method: Direct application of claim 6, with 41,502 exact finite gap checks on graph pairs through n=4.

claims.claim: Any FP solver at fixed c yields a polynomial-time additive-2⌊n/c⌋ approximation for Minimum Dominating Set.
claims.evidence: Let R=⌊n/c⌋ and query every q. At q0=min(n,γ(G)+R), every permitted H satisfies γ(H)≤γ(G)+R when q0<n, while q0=n is always feasible; hence the first YES threshold q* is at most q0. Transferring its q*-set back to G by claim 6 adds at most R vertices, producing size at most γ(G)+2R. There are only n+1 solver calls.
claims.search_method: Full algorithmic proof; the transfer and Lipschitz ingredients were exhaustively checked on all graph pairs through n=4.

claims.claim: On graphs of maximum degree Δ, the preceding algorithm is a (1+2(Δ+1)/c)-approximation.
claims.evidence: Each chosen vertex dominates at most Δ+1 vertices, so n≤(Δ+1)γ(G). Claim 8 gives output size at most γ(G)+2⌊n/c⌋≤γ(G)+2n/c≤(1+2(Δ+1)/c)γ(G). The empty graph is handled exactly.
claims.search_method: Counting proof with integer cross-multiplied checks for all graphs through n=5 and multiple rational c values.

claims.claim: There is an exact approximation-preserving reduction from isolate-free Vertex Cover of maximum degree three to Dominating Set of maximum degree six.
claims.evidence: For every edge uv, retain uv and add x_uv adjacent to u and v. A vertex cover dominates all x_uv and, because the input is isolate-free, every uncovered original vertex. Conversely, replacing each selected x_uv by an endpoint never increases size; the resulting original-only set covers uv because it must dominate x_uv. Thus γ equals the cover number, solutions transfer without loss, original degrees double to at most six, and new vertices have degree two.
claims.search_method: Direct gadget proof plus exhaustive checks of 558 isolate-free degree-three inputs through five vertices and 362,528 dominating-set conversions.

claims.claim: The universal target implies a PTAS family for cubic Minimum Vertex Cover.
claims.evidence: For fixed ε>0 choose c=14/ε. Claims 8 and 9 give a (1+14/c)=(1+ε) dominating-set approximation on the degree-six gadget, and claim 10 converts it to a no-larger vertex cover with the same optimum. Isolated input vertices may simply be removed. For each fixed ε the solver and resulting algorithm are polynomial-time, which is precisely a PTAS family.
claims.search_method: Deductive composition of the verified approximation bound and exact gadget reduction.

claims.claim: Conditional on the standard APX-hardness theorem for cubic Vertex Cover, the universal target holds if and only if P=NP.
claims.evidence: Under the stated APX-hardness hypothesis, there is η>0 such that a polynomial (1+η)-approximation for cubic Vertex Cover implies P=NP. The universal target supplies a solver with c>14/η, and claim 11 then violates that gap unless P=NP. Conversely, if P=NP, Dominating Set decision and witness construction are polynomial; one can output H=G, extend a solution to exactly q vertices when feasible, and otherwise output nil, using zero edits for every c.
claims.search_method: Logical implication with the APX-hardness gap theorem treated exactly as the claim's explicit hypothesis.

target_evidence: The exact target requests an unconditional algorithm for every fixed c>0. The draft rigorously proves the full sidestep requirement only for 0<c≤e and gives correct triage, direct certificates, and approximation consequences beyond that range. Its equivalence with P=NP is conditional and does not settle the remaining unconditional c>e regime. This is material but incomplete progress, so target_verdict is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS. Separately, claimed_resolution is PARTIAL and the final writeup explicitly disclaims an all-c unconditional resolution; that claimed resolution is ACCURATE.
